title: Signed Wire application completion uses General ooRexx Deployment dev4 live evidence
summary: Candidate 4 adds a native fail-closed completion gate that consumes the common HostedModuleEvidence. The candidate is locally qualified, not installed or running. The gate prevents an unprobed candidate from being marked PROBED_ACTIVE through the intended hosted workflow.
contract: wire.deployment.command/0.1 -> WAPP_ADMIT -> HostedModuleEvidence -> separately verified HTTPS/WSS/LDAP semantic probe -> WAPP_COMPLETE(PROBED_ACTIVE)
boundaries: Rasen Falcon site/HTTPS/LDAP deployment still requires actual host installation, independent authenticated live verification and no unapproved production cutover.

Only the common General Deployment HostedModuleEvidence is authoritative for stage/load/composition/activation/probe state; do not infer a live app from Queue Fabric ACK, a staged ZIP or an HTTP connection.
The app delivery request must match immutable admitted digest and target, application and generation, mount path, and trusted Storage Fabric evidence reference.

A separate host-injected verifier must independently attest HTTPS/TLS, WSS semantic action/observation and applicable LDAP policy. Local tests use fake authority; they do not certify production TLS or LDAP.
The underlying journal complete() remains privileged. The adapter does not remove raw journal access; host composition must prevent untrusted code from acquiring it.
gates: real signed .wapp verifier, content-addressed Storage Fabric fetch and approved target policy
native host attestation for private-CA HTTPS/WSS plus actual Wire semantic action and observation
LDAP bind, search and revocation enforcement on the same selected host
multi-writer fencing, power-loss journal durability and restart replay in production
integration retest against latest accepted General Deployment and website publishing code
